headline: Energy Markets Spike As Natural Gas Crosses Key Threshold And Oil Reacts To Geopolitics
paragraphs: Natural gas surged 12.42 percent daily and 8.44 percent weekly to EUR 2.72 per MMBtu, driven by fears of an Iran war escalation and European gas prices topping EUR 100 for the first time since 2022. Brent crude fell 2.63 percent following reports of oil gushing out of the Gulf, while WTI crude gained 2.21 percent after a Saudi Arabian refinery attack. The euro traded at 1.1153 against the dollar, remaining a stable baseline for Irish businesses tracking these import costs.

Precious metals and industrial inputs saw notable shifts tied to macroeconomic policy and supply dynamics. Silver dropped 0.82 percent daily and 1.67 percent weekly as a rejection at the $55 level put $50 back in focus. Palladium slipped 0.85 percent daily and 3.48 percent weekly, entering an oversold zone amid high-impact market conditions. Copper rose 4.64 percent on the week, supported by the World Bank lifting its copper price outlook by 18 percent and strong Chinese demand premiums.

Gold edged down 0.18 percent to EUR 3646.65 per oz, pressured as the Federal Reserve voted 10 to 2 in favor of a rate hold, with the Iran war lifting yields and the dollar. Platinum dipped 2.04 percent over the week.
